segments.EST.1.1-2: Xerxes rules 127 provinces from his throne in Susa
segments.EST.1.3-4: Xerxes shows his riches to his officials for 180 days
segments.EST.1.5-6: Xerxes gives a seven-day feast for all people in Susa
segments.EST.1.7-8: At the feast, the king lets every man drink freely
segments.EST.1.9-11: Xerxes orders eunuchs to bring Queen Vashti to him
segments.EST.1.12-12: Queen Vashti refuses to come, and the king is furious
segments.EST.1.13-15: Xerxes asks his advisors what to do about Vashti
segments.EST.1.16-18: Memucan warns that wives will despise husbands
segments.EST.1.19-20: Memucan advises a decree to remove Vashti as queen
segments.EST.1.21-22: Xerxes sends letters that every man must rule his home
segments.EST.2.1-2: Xerxes’ attendants suggest a search for young women
segments.EST.2.3-4: Xerxes plans to choose a new queen from young women
segments.EST.2.5-6: Mordecai is a Jewish man living in Susa
segments.EST.2.7-7: Mordecai raises his cousin Esther as his own daughter
segments.EST.2.8-9: Esther is taken to the palace and Hegai favors her
segments.EST.2.10-11: Esther does not reveal her people, as Mordecai said
segments.EST.2.12-13: Each young woman receives a year of beauty treatments
segments.EST.2.14-14: A young woman goes to the king and then to a second harem
segments.EST.2.15-16: Esther gains favor and goes to King Xerxes
segments.EST.2.17-18: Xerxes makes Esther queen and holds a great banquet
segments.EST.2.19-20: Esther still keeps her people secret, as Mordecai said
segments.EST.2.21-21: Two guards plan to kill King Xerxes
segments.EST.2.22-23: Mordecai reports the plot and the two guards are hanged
segments.EST.3.1-2: The king honors Haman, but Mordecai will not bow
segments.EST.3.3-4: The king’s servants tell Haman that Mordecai disobeys
segments.EST.3.5-6: Haman is angry and plans to destroy all the Jews
segments.EST.3.7-7: Haman casts lots to choose a day and month
segments.EST.3.8-9: Haman asks King Xerxes to destroy the Jews
segments.EST.3.10-11: The king gives Haman his ring and power over the Jews
segments.EST.3.12-13: Haman’s order to kill all the Jews is written and sent
segments.EST.3.14-15: The edict is sent out and Susa is in confusion
segments.EST.4.1-3: Mordecai and the Jews mourn because of the edict
segments.EST.4.4-5: Esther sends Hathach to ask Mordecai what is wrong
segments.EST.4.6-8: Mordecai asks Esther to plead with the king for the Jews
segments.EST.4.9-12: Esther tells Mordecai she may not go to the king
segments.EST.4.13-14: Mordecai tells Esther she must not stay silent
segments.EST.5.1-2: The king welcomes Esther with his gold scepter
segments.EST.5.3-4: Esther invites the king and Haman to a banquet
segments.EST.5.5-6: At the banquet the king asks Esther what she wants
segments.EST.5.7-8: Esther invites the king and Haman to a second banquet
segments.EST.5.9-11: Haman is angry at Mordecai and boasts to his friends
segments.EST.5.12-13: Haman says Mordecai’s presence spoils all his joy
segments.EST.5.14-14: Haman’s wife and friends tell him to build a gallows
segments.EST.6.1-3: The king learns that Mordecai was never rewarded
segments.EST.6.4-6: The king asks Haman how to honor a man
segments.EST.6.7-9: Haman describes how the king should honor a man
segments.EST.6.10-11: The king orders Haman to honor Mordecai
segments.EST.6.12-14: Haman goes home in grief and is taken to the banquet
segments.EST.7.1-2: The king asks Esther again what she wants
segments.EST.7.3-5: Esther asks the king to save her and her people
segments.EST.7.6-6: Esther names Haman as the enemy
segments.EST.7.7-7: The angry king leaves, and Haman begs Esther for his life
segments.EST.7.8-8: The king sees Haman fall on Esther’s couch
segments.EST.7.9-10: Haman is hanged on the gallows he made for Mordecai
segments.EST.8.1-2: The king honors Esther and Mordecai
segments.EST.8.3-4: Esther weeps and begs the king to stop Haman’s plan
segments.EST.8.5-6: Esther asks the king to cancel Haman’s letters
segments.EST.8.7-8: The king lets Mordecai write a new decree for the Jews
segments.EST.8.9-9: Mordecai’s orders are written to all 127 provinces
segments.EST.8.10-12: The decree lets the Jews defend themselves on one day
segments.EST.8.13-14: Couriers carry the decree to every province quickly
segments.EST.8.15-17: Mordecai leaves the king, and the Jews rejoice
segments.EST.9.1-2: On the thirteenth day, the Jews overpower enemies
segments.EST.9.3-5: Officials help the Jews, who defeat all enemies
segments.EST.9.6-10: The Jews kill 500 men and Haman’s ten sons in Susa
segments.EST.9.11-12: The king asks Esther what more she wants
segments.EST.9.13-14: Esther asks for one more day, and Haman’s sons are hanged
segments.EST.9.15-16: The Jews kill more enemies in Susa and the provinces
segments.EST.9.17-17: The Jews rest on the fourteenth day with feasting
segments.EST.9.18-19: Jews in Susa and in villages rest on different days
segments.EST.9.20-22: Mordecai tells the Jews to celebrate two days each year
segments.EST.9.23-25: The Jews continue the custom because Haman’s plot failed
segments.EST.9.26-28: The days are called Purim and are to be kept every year
segments.EST.9.29-29: Esther and Mordecai write a second letter about Purim
segments.EST.9.30-32: Mordecai sends letters to confirm the days of Purim
segments.EST.10.1-2: King Xerxes taxes the land; Mordecai’s deeds are recorded
segments.EST.10.3-3: Mordecai is second only to King Xerxes and helps the Jews
